title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA kernel & KV-cache tuning
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Optimize kernel selection and KV-cache layout for Llama/Mistral/Qwen; reduce p99 latency and token cost for GQA/MQA models. No API changes.
description: Motivation: several open tickets and perf regressions showed that one-size-fits-all kernel selection and KV-cache layouts cause suboptimal latency for models with Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) variants (notably Qwen and recent Mistral/Llama forks). This PR introduces model-specific heuristics and micro-optimizations in the serving runtime: 1) a lightweight kernel selector that prefers MQA/GQA-aware fused kernels when signatures match; 2) KV-cache packing changes to avoid cache-line fragmentation for per-head vs multi-query layouts; 3) scheduler hints to prefer single-request fast-path on latency-sensitive routes while retaining continuous batching for high-throughput routes; 4) small math-kernel adjustments (transposed GEMM paths and attention softmax numerics) to reduce transient allocations that impacted p99. The change is guarded by model-profiles in the registry and defaults to previous behavior for unknown models, enabling safe rollout. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes; behavior can be toggled per-deployment via runtime flags. Validation: microbenchmarks across Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B showed 12-28% p99 latency reductions and 6-14% token-cost improvement on our standard throughput traces. See commits and CI checks below for details.
